Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

section.title: Purpose
section.s: N-25 is the one writer of the GitHub commit status coq/gate on a head sha: success when every planned unit passed, failure when a unit failed, error when the infrastructure ran out or a newer head superseded the run; with the required status check on main (D05, ruling C43) GitHub itself refuses a merge without a green gate, and an agent can read the verdict but never edit it.
It closes the loop the investigation found open: no status had ever been posted, main required no check, and the only gate was a script reading records (RC3 item 7, RC7, L07 section 5 item 3).

Input to output: the set of pod.run records (N-24) and check.verdict records (N-46) for one head sha and plan attempt starts it; the posted status plus a gate.run record ends it; N-04 sees the status on its next poll and N-08 reads the verdict from the snapshot.

section.title: Input records: pod.run and check.verdict for one head sha

record.s: The node reads the newest suite.plan (or main.plan) for the head sha and attempt, and the result record per entry: pod.run for kind pod (N-24), check.verdict for kind spec-check (N-46); the input is complete when every entry has a result record or the plan's bound has passed.
record.field: The pull request or 0 for main.
name, kind, code, outcome, log per entry.

section.title: Output: the coq/gate commit status and the gate.run record
section.s: The status: POST /repos/jkkelley/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/statuses/<head_sha> with context coq/gate, state pending while the plan runs, then success, failure or error, a description of at most 140 characters (N pods passed; <unit> failed plus K more; infrastructure failed after the ladder: <reason>; superseded by <sha12>; plan refused: <reason>), and target_url the gate page link.

record.field: The attempt whose results this verdict is from.
pass, fail, timeout, infra, superseded, spec_check_pass, spec_check_fail.
name and log of the unit the description names.
GitHub status id, created_at, and attempts used to post.

section.s: The gate page link: the Jenkins build page of the plan's build (http://jenkins.homelab.local/job/coq-gate/N/) which holds every unit log and is reachable on the owner's LAN and tailnet; the bearings page (N-32) also shows the gate.run record per pull request, and the map's machine screen (N-39) links both.

section.title: Mechanism: the verdict rule, the status post, the page link, supersession, the required check
section.step: When N-23 or N-26 writes the plan with a build number, this node posts coq/gate pending with description "running N units" (idempotency key repo:head_sha:pending:attempt); when a plan is refused (412) it posts error with the refusal's reason, so the worker sees why there is no run.

The verdict rule, pure over the result set (finish() of coqGate.groovy, moved into the Go service): any result with outcome infra or code 500 and no later successful attempt available means error; else any fail, timeout or check fail means failure, and the description names the first failing unit by plan order plus the count of the rest; else every entry has a pass and the state is success with the pod count; a result set with a superseded unit is error superseded; an empty plan (nothing to run) is success "nothing to run".

Error from infrastructure is not final at once: the gate run has up to 3 plan attempts; on infra the node asks N-23 (or N-26) to trigger the plan again as attempt n plus 1 with N-11's backoff, and the status stays pending with "retrying attempt n plus 1"; after the third attempt's infra the status is error and one card is posted by N-28 (dedupe key node:N-25:head_sha).

The post: GitHub REST with the Go service's token, 3 tries with 2 s, 4 s, 8 s backoff, a 10 s timeout each; before posting, the node reads the current status from the newest forge.snapshot (N-04) and skips the post when state and description already match (idempotent on content); every post writes the gate.run record with the GitHub status id.

Supersession: N-07's tick compares each open pull request's head in forge.snapshot with the newest plan; when the head moved, N-07 writes plan.superseded 410 for the old sha, the Go service stops the old build, and this node posts error "superseded by <new sha12>" on the old sha, so no sha is ever left pending (the abortPrevious semantic of the old Jenkinsfile, now owned by the scheduler).

The required check: at every service start and daily tick, ci/bin/branch-protection.sh --check reads GET /repos/.../branches/main/protection and asserts required_status_checks.contexts contains coq/gate with strict true (the head must be up to date with main, so the gate ran on what merges); when it does not, the script applies it (PUT, 3 tries) and writes protection.applied 200; a failure to apply after 3 tries is protection.failed 500 and one card, and N-09 refuses to merge while no protection.applied exists (shared need for G2).
gate.run is the record N-08 may also read, but the authority is the status on GitHub (D05): N-08 reads coq/gate from forge.snapshot; gate.run is the derived notification and the audit trail.
section.mermaid: flowchart LR P[plan with build number] --> S0[post coq/gate pending] R[every entry has a pod.run or check.verdict] --> V{verdict rule} V -- all pass --> OK[post success; gate.run 201] V -- a fail or timeout --> F[post failure naming the unit; gate.run 422] V -- infra and attempts left --> A[re-trigger plan attempt n+1; pending] V -- infra after 3 --> E[post error; gate.run 500; one card] N[newer head on the same PR] --> X[stop old build; post error superseded; gate.run 410] OK --> N04[N-04 poll sees the status] F --> N04 E --> N04 X --> N04 N04 --> N08[N-08 gate check reads the verdict]
section.s: The merge path after this node: N-08 reads green, N-19's review.passed lands on the same head, N-09 merges by machine (D15, ruling C50); GitHub enforces the check independently of every record.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.s: N-07 dispatches the verdict as a system job under the plan's lease when every entry of a plan attempt has a result record, or when the plan's bound has passed (then the missing results are infra, N-24 section waits w6); the comparison is level-triggered, so a result that arrives late or a crash before the post is settled on the next tick.
The pending post is dispatched by the same rule the moment a plan has a build number.
At service start, every plan with results and no gate.run of the same attempt is re-evaluated; a status already on GitHub is read from the snapshot and not re-posted.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: The plan's bound (sum of budgets divided by maxPods plus 30 minutes, capped at PT3H) from the build start.
wait.fallback: Missing results become infra (N-24 writes them with reason result-missing); the verdict rule runs on what exists; attempts and the card as in section retries.

wait.timeout: 10 s per call, 3 calls with backoff.
wait.fallback: The gate.run is written with posted.ok false and the next tick retries the post (the status content is the idempotency key, so a late success is harmless); after 3 ticks of failure status.post.failed 500 and one card; the verdict record exists either way so N-08 can read gate.run as a fallback when the snapshot has no status after PT10M (shared need for G2).

wait.on: The old build stopping on supersession.
wait.timeout: 60 s for POST /stop to take effect, polled on the build's building flag.
wait.fallback: The status on the old sha is posted regardless; a build that keeps running ends on its own bound and its results are written as superseded 410 and ignored.
protection.failed 500, one card; N-09 refuses merges until protection.applied exists.

section.title: Retries, recovery and the report
section.s: Infrastructure results re-trigger the plan up to 3 attempts in total (the pod ladder inside each attempt is separate and bounded); test failures never re-trigger anything.
The post retries 3 times per tick and across 3 ticks, then reports with one card; nothing loops, because the content key makes every retry the same post.
After the third infra attempt the status is error with the reason and one card; the pull request stays red until a new head; the worker lane sees the reason on the pull request and in the record.
Recovery after a crash: records and the GitHub status are the only state; the start comparison re-posts what is missing and skips what is present.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.s: One writer: only the Go service holds the GitHub token with repo:status; seats are rendered without it (N-13) and the reviewer reads gh pr checks; a seat cannot post, edit or delete a status, which is the T04 property the field calls a verdict the agent reads and cannot change.

Many heads at once: statuses are per sha and the key includes the sha and attempt; two pull requests never share a status; two attempts of one sha post in attempt order because the verdict job holds the plan lease.
Two Go service instances: the lease's fencing token; the loser's gate.run put is a 409 and its post is skipped because the content check sees the winner's status.

A seat that pushes while the gate runs: the new head is planned, the old run is superseded and says so on the old sha; the reviewer reading the pull request sees pending on the new head and never a stale green.

The reviewer and the gate on one head: review.passed and coq/gate are independent records on the same sha; N-09 requires both; neither waits on the other, so a review posted before green simply waits in the store.
Collision answer in one line: single status writer with a lease per plan, content-keyed idempotent posts, per-sha statuses, supersession owned by the scheduler, 409 on a stale writer.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.emits: The status pending was posted; nobody acts.
coq/gate success; N-08 reads green; N-09 may merge with review.passed.
coq/gate failure; the worker lane acts on the named unit's log; a new head re-enters.
coq/gate error after 3 attempts; N-28 posts one card.
coq/gate error plan refused (fork, no image, planner error); the worker lane acts.
The required check is set; N-09 reads it as its precondition.
One card each; N-09 refuses merges on protection.failed.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each
section.path: The verdict input set and the post request and response bodies, for audit.

path.cleanup: kept on purpose: GitHub keeps statuses with the commit; nothing to delete, and a status is never edited after a terminal state

section.path: Not a host path; listed so the rule holds.
Removing the required check is a one-time owner action; the daily check re-applies it unless a ruling record says otherwise.
section.s: The script dry-runs by default, acts with --apply, retries 3 times and exits 4 listing what remains; N-45 registers it.

section.title: DAG edges in and out
section.out: The posted status appears in the next forge.snapshot.

item.check: coq/gate is a required status check on main with strict true.
item.proof: branch-protection.sh --check exit 0 in the daily tick record and gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection showing the context.

item.check: Every planned head ends with a terminal status: no sha stays pending past its bound.
item.proof: A daily query over forge.snapshot: zero heads with coq/gate pending older than PT3H; the alert in section monitoring.

item.check: The verdict rule is pure and tested: success, first failure named, infra error, superseded, empty plan.
item.proof: Go unit tests in the service package for the rule with the five fixtures; go test exit 0 in the scheduler suite's pod.run.

item.check: A post is idempotent on content.
item.proof: Scenario repost in the fake forge: two verdict runs on one result set produce one status.

item.check: A newer head supersedes the old run and the old sha reads error superseded.
item.proof: Scenario supersede: old sha status error with the new sha12 in the description; the old build's stop was called.

item.check: No seat holds a token that can post a status.
item.proof: The rendered settings of every role (N-13) deny gh api on statuses; a reviewer run that tries is refused with 412 in its seat.result.

item.check: The target_url opens the build with the unit logs.
item.proof: A GET on the target_url from the tailnet returns 200 and lists units/*.log.

item.check: The first live pull request after cut-over carries a coq/gate status.
item.proof: gh pr checks on that pull request shows coq/gate with a state; the gate.run record id in the ledger.

section.title: Permissions
section.s: The Go service: a fine-grained GitHub token with commit statuses write, contents read, pull requests read, administration write for branch protection on this repository only, read from the host keyring, never in a record or an environment a seat inherits.
Jenkins: no GitHub token for the gate; its only GitHub credential is the GHCR push secret in N-22's job.
Seats: read statuses through gh pr checks (the rendered settings allow gh pr view and gh pr checks); no write.
The owner: may remove the required check as break glass with the script; the next daily tick re-applies it unless a ruling record (N-29) with kind protection.waiver and an expiry exists.

section.title: Monitoring
section.s: Status fields: pending heads and their age, verdicts by state in the last 24 h, post failures, attempts used per head, time from pr.opened to a terminal status (p50 and p95), protection state.
Alerts (N-41): a head pending past its bound; status.post.failed; protection.failed or the context missing; verdict error rate above 10 percent in a day (infrastructure trouble).
Map: N-25 is the lamp on every pull request item on the belt; the stats screen shows time-to-verdict.

section.title: Runbook
section.step: A red pull request: the description names the unit; the log is behind the target_url and in the pod.run record; the fix is a new commit, which replans; nobody re-runs a failed assertion.
An error status: superseded needs nothing; infrastructure after the ladder has a card; the N-24 runbook names the cause classes.
Protection missing or failed: the daily tick re-applies; if the token lacks administration write the card says so and the owner updates the token once.
A deliberate bypass (owner only): a ruling record protection.waiver with an expiry; the script honours it until the expiry and then re-applies.
